title: Behavior‑First Hosted Endpoints PRD + Launch Readiness Checklist
creator: Aisha Raman
description: PRD to define behavior-first contracts for the hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank), plus a prescriptive launch readiness checklist that ties acceptance criteria to telemetry and rollback gates. This ticket coordinates PM/Eng/Design/QA to ensure launch does not regress existing consumers and provides deterministic behavior guarantees for common integration patterns.
background: Multiple teams have reported subtle behavioral drift between model variants and endpoint wrappers during previous launches (notably at the chat-completions boundary and embedding normalization). Current product docs focus on surface and params, but lack concrete behavioral contracts (e.g., deterministic seeding, tokenization compatibility, structured output stability). This PRD creates explicit, measurable guarantees and a checklist to reduce regressions during canaries and regional rollouts.
goals: Define clear behavioral contracts for each endpoint type (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank).
Specify measurable acceptance criteria tied to telemetry and synthetic evals.
Provide a step-by-step launch readiness checklist: canary gates, monitoring dashboards, and rollback criteria.
Align SDK/Docs/Console UI to reflect behavioral guarantees and migration notes.
scope_in_scope: Behavioral contract doc for chat: conversation turn stability, system prompt handling, function call determinism.
Behavioral contract doc for completions: stop token semantics, sampling defaults, max_tokens edge cases.
Embedding contract: vector normalization, stable dimensionality, version tags, and small perturbation guarantees.
Rerank contract: input ranking determinism for identical signals, tie-breaking rules, and top-k stability.
Launch readiness checklist and canary gating rules (metrics + thresholds).
Developer-facing migration notes and SDK changes where behavior differs.
out_of_scope: Major inference runtime changes that alter model interfaces (these should be separate ENG epics).
Re-architecting Dedicated or Private deployment modes — this ticket only affects hosted API contracts and docs.
Model training or fine-tuning to change model semantics; we address rollout of model variants only insofar as behavioral guarantees require transforms/wrappers.
acceptance_criteria: All behavioral contracts published in the internal Confluence page and linked in public API docs (if customer-facing) before canary start.
Synthetic regression suite passes: no more than 0.5% significant-answer-change rate on 10k seeded prompts for chat/completions between baseline and candidate variants.
Embeddings stability: cosine similarity between baseline and candidate for a canonical corpus >= 0.995 after normalization (unless model intentionally changed).
Rerank stability: identical inputs produce the same order at >= 99.5% parity; documented tie-breaking behavior for equal scores.
Latency and error SLOs validated in staging: p95 <= production target + 10% and error-rate delta <= 0.1%.
SDKs and example notebooks updated with explicit behavior notes and migration examples; docs reviewed and approved by DevRel.
Operational dashboards instrumented: per-route behavioral regression metric, drift alert, token distribution histograms, and rollback playbook available.
Security review completed for any changes that touch request/response transformations (KMS/PII handling) and signed off by Security.
rollout_plan: Pre-canary: publish contracts and run 10k synthetic checks in staging; run a subset of customer prompts from the privacy-safe corpus.
Canary-1 (low traffic, single region): 1% of traffic for 48 hours; monitor behavioral regression metric and latency/error SLOs.
Canary-2 (regional expansion): 10% traffic across 2 regions for 24 hours; escalate if any drift or error thresholds breached.
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h observation windows, abort or rollback if any canary gate fails.
Post-launch: 7-day regression watch with daily summary and a postmortem template ready in case of incidents.
risks_mitigation: Risk: subtle semantic changes between model variants causing user-visible regressions. Mitigation: large seeded synthetic suite + small customer shadowing before canary.
Risk: telemetry blind spots. Mitigation: instrument per-route semantic drift metrics and token distribution charts before canary.
Risk: SDKs not surface behavior changes. Mitigation: ship clear migration examples and set docs as a gating criteria for launch.
open_questions: Do we treat small, intentional semantic deltas (e.g., safety-improved responses) as regressions or as documented behavior changes? (PM/Legal/Safety decision needed).
Which existing customer accounts should be included in shadowing with opt-in? (security & privacy review required).
Are the synthetic thresholds above the right sensitivity for rare but high-impact regressions? Engineering input requested.
